III to its mouth on the south bank of the Yellowstone River near Hysham. Sarpy Creek and its tributaries drain the eastern two-thirds of Tract II and all of Tract III. The total Sarpy Creek drainage is 453 square miles in extent, of which about 40 square miles or 8.8 percent, are within Tracts II and III. The drainage areas of Sarpy Creek and East Fork Sarpy Creek measured at their confluence are 76.3 and 80.7 miles respectively.
With the exception of the Middle Fork of Sarpy Creek in the southern portion of Tract III, all drainages located within the tracts originate within the boundaries of those leases and drain relatively small areas, generally less than five square miles. The Middle Fork of Sarpy Creek (sometimes referred to as Spring Creek) drains approximately 12 square miles, five of which are located upstream from the lease boundary. The main channels of drainages located entirely within the lease boundaries are relatively straight in their upper reaches, but Sarpy and Tullock Creeks tend to meander in broad valleys. Channel gradients are generally between 10 and 20 feet per mile. These drainage basins are relatively free from natural or manmade impoundments.
Streamflow - All streams located within Tracts II and III are intermittent and flow only as a result of direct runoff from intensive spring and summer storms and snowmelt. Because most channel bottoms are located above the water table, no base flow and little, if any, springflow is introduced into the channels from the alluvium. Outside of the lease boundary, continuous flow has been observed in several channels including Sarpy Creek, Pleasant Creek, and both the East and Middle Forks of Sarpy Creek.
